name: Chimpanzee Visitant
source: Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God

generalAbilities.name: Lifesense (Imprecise) 60 feet
generalAbilities.description:
See rules...

Lifesense allows a monster to sense the vital essence of living and undead creatures within the listed range. The sense can distinguish between the vitality energy animating living creatures and the void energy animating undead creatures, much as sight distinguishes colors.

defensiveAbilities.name: Vengeful Presence
defensiveAbilities.description:
20 feet. A creature that starts its turn within the visitant's aura must succeed at a DC 16 Will Saving Throw save or be overcome with a thirst for vengeance.

For 1d4 rounds (1 minute on a critical failure), if the affected creature was attacked within the last round (whether or not the attack hit), the creature must use at least 1 action per round to Strike or use a hostile action toward its last attacker as long as the attacker is still alive. Failure to do so deals the affected creature 1d6 Mental Damage damage.

defensiveAbilities.name: Void Healing
defensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

defensiveAbilities.name: Whip Vulnerability
defensiveAbilities.description: A chimpanzee visitant takes 5 Slashing Damage{5} additional damage from whips.

offensiveAbilities.name: Mauler
offensiveAbilities.description: The visitant gains a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against a creature it has Grabbed.

offensiveAbilities.name: Rabies
offensiveAbilities.description:
Visitants can be carriers of diseases, even if they are immune to their effects.

Saving Throw DC 16 Fortitude Saving Throw.

Stage 1 Sickened 1 (1 day)

Stage 2 Sickened 2 (1 day)

Stage 3 Confusion (1 day)

Stage 4 dead

offensiveAbilities.name: Grab
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.
